item.title: Heavy Metal, 1981 - ★★★★
item.description: Short vignettes of good against evil taking place across the universe, told through the lens of a nerdy, comic book loving, heavy metal listening lens. I find the art style quite unique and enjoy the stories, especially the cyberpunk story set in futuristic dystopian New York, which is in a long line of inspiration for the likes of Blade Runner, Akira, Fifth Element, etc. The audio quality is great if you’re in the mood for some hard rock. The low frequency channel goes nuts in this movie. And if you have a short attention span there’s naked women with big boobs every 10 minutes.
item.dc:creator: dylan_fisher

item.title: Vertigo, 1958 - ★★★★
item.description: Without a doubt a fantastic film, but I found the pacing and wax statue-like demeanor of the protagonist to be a bit dull. Highlights for me include the deep and vibrant colors, the masterful compositions of on location San Francisco shots, — especially the wide landscapes, the trippy nightmare scenes and animation halfway through the movie, and the quintessential Hitchcock story that keeps evolving in new and unusual ways.
item.dc:creator: dylan_fisher

item.title: New Rose Hotel, 1998 - ★★½
item.description:
Strange movie, very gestural. Part music video, part espionage thriller — but you never see the action. The movie is made up of fringe moments and you are left to piece together the puzzle. Feels like an exercise in male dominance over women, lots of male gaze going on.

There are some redeeming visual moments. And the audio is consistent, made up of a subdued and dreary soundtrack interspersed with what sounds like field recordings or sound collages in between. It creates a melancholic and uneasy atmosphere. Visually it’s a pretty good looking movie. Christopher Walken is exciting, but kind of eclipses Willem Dafoe — maybe that’s intentional.

The portrayal of technology is interesting. Some funky cell phone visualizations, CCTV captures, and a laughable interface for checking your Swiss bank account.

I could see this appealing to some. Kind of has a Lynch vibe to it.
item.dc:creator: dylan_fisher
